verdict: Better than home_r2, but the stage is still split, and the four screen cameras are what keep it below a fern film. The dining set (the cold dining, dining_gene, chair and chair_gene, and the warm dining_family) is near fern level: motivated stripes, real shadows, one clear subject. Of the screen angles, kitchen_over is the best. It has clean corners, Dawn's face reflected in the glass pass, and a black bezel, and it cuts with the front kitchen view on colour, mug side and light direction. Its keyboard reads pale, though: the glossy well between the keys mirrors the screen. The front kitchen frame works as a beat. Its laptop lid, though, is a raw 0.0 black card covering about 5% of the frame (7% with the unlit table under it). tv is no longer a grey card filling the frame, but it still does not read as a lit television in a family's room. The TV is about 28% of the frame width and hangs beside a picture frame of about the same size, at nearly the same height, so it reads as a second, blank picture. The brightest wall (graded about 73) is under the picture, about 1 m from the TV's centre, while the wall right of the TV grades about 21. The only surface the screen visibly lights is the side wall just past the TV's end, and a dark wedge at the corner cuts that glow off from the set. The foreground "chair" exists only in this camera, and it does not look like the slatted dining chairs. tv_insert is technically clean: screen corners 91-216 px from the edges, a black bezel at 7-15 graded, a 65-level antialiased matte. As a picture, though, it is a flat 16:9 card. Its glass pass reflects a flat trapezoid "window" with no blind slats, in the room whose identity is the blinds.
answers:
1) Do the screen, cabinet and soft foreground chair read as one room? Not yet. The sideboard, vase, brass candlesticks, framed picture and wall colour match chair.jpg (its back wall grades about 36/43/55; tv's wall runs from about 25/29/38 to 62/73/85 across the frame). So the cabinet does tie tv to the dining set. Four things break it:
(a) "tv foreground chair" at (2.30, -0.90) is hidden in every other framing (`part.hide_render = framing != "tv"`). It stands 0.5 m from where round 2 removed chair_n2 (2.42, -0.42) to clear the near side of the dining wide. Projected into the dining camera, its back would stand in the wide's lower centre (top rail at about x 530, y 530, 1.4 m from the lens). Cut dining to tv and a chair appears that was not in the room.
(b) That chair does not read as the room's chairs. At 0.9 m and f/4 its slatted back blurs into one rounded slab, dark red-brown in the raw (about rgb 15/9/10), graded 9 with a 25 top edge. It looks like the back of an upholstered sofa, not a spindle-back dining chair. It also lacks the satin_wood finish the other dining chairs get. (The sat 0.72 / val 0.78 are its build arguments, not its rendered colour.)
(c) The camera sits at (2.71, -0.10, 1.02), inside the dining table's footprint (x 1.9-3.7, y -0.485 to 0.485) and 27 cm above its top. No seated person could have that eye line, and the table that defines the room is never seen: its far edge projects about 450 px below the frame.
(d) About four-fifths of the TV's width (x 1.15-1.92 of its 1.15-2.09) hangs past the sideboard's end over bare wall. In frame the foreground chair hides where the sideboard ends, so the TV's right part floats over wall with nothing under it.

2) Does the case read as black and recessed? Black, yes. In the room view all four bezel sides grade about 7-12 (raw 2-7). The top bezel does not catch light; the 31-36 line above it is wall. On the insert the left, right and bottom bezel grade 7-11, with the top at about 15. Recessed only on the insert: the 6 mm lip shows as a second inner line along the top bezel at 2x. In the room view, at about 340 px wide, the 44 mm case shows no depth and no lit edge. It casts no shadow or occlusion on the wall in either camera (the insert wall reads 22-34 all round). So it reads as a black frame flat on the wall, not as an object standing about 5 cm proud of it.

3) The spill A/B. Your numbers hold roughly. The wall right of the TV grades about 21, and the wall between it and the picture 40-50, depending on the patch. But the pool you raised is in the wrong place. "tv_return" sits at (2.03, -1.55, 1.36), aimed at (2.61, -2.03, 1.04), about 1 m from the TV centre (x 1.62). So the brightest wall in the frame (graded about 73) is between the candlesticks under the picture.
There is a second glow on the side wall at the right edge (raw about 105-145, graded 50-60), and it does have a source. It is most likely tv_spill: the TV's end is only 15 cm from that wall, and no other light reaches it with any strength. The spill's 150-degree spread cuts off just short of the corner, which leaves a dark wedge between the TV and the glow, so the glow reads as detached rather than as the screen's light.
tv_spill has visible_glossy False and specular 0, so the brass candlesticks get no cool edge from the screen. The sideboard top (graded about 25) could not mirror the screen from this eye line anyway. The candlesticks throw no visible shadow away from the TV. Apart from the side-wall glow, nothing in the frame says the light comes from the screen.

4) Dawn's hands across the kitchen cut. They work at cutting speed but not invisibly. In the over-the-shoulder, her right hand is curled over the keys right of centre, fingertips on rows 2-4. Whatever the 3.15 mm pad clearance, no trackpad reads from this angle; its material (0.075) is nearly the deck's (0.070). Her left hand lies with its fingers straight out across the keys, the index straightest, its tip on about the third (home) row. In the front view her right hand is raised with the index pointing straight down at the deck and the other fingers tucked behind it, a pointer pose; her left hand is hidden by the lid. The stiff, straight index in both angles is what reads as posed. Wrists 23-24 mm above the deck read fine.

5) The darker laptop deck. In the over-the-shoulder the palm rest grades about 84 median and the key tops about 100-115. The brightest things on the keyboard are the gaps between the keys, at 160-175. The keyboard well uses the glossy bezel glass (roughness 0.08-0.14) and mirrors the lit screen as a pale grid, with a pale rectangle where the arrow cluster leaves the well bare. That reads as a pale keyboard on a space-grey laptop. In the front view the lid back is raw 0.0, graded 4-7: no light, no rim, a hole. One machine, two looks, so the cut shows a change of object. On a black laptop the keys and the gaps between them should be the darkest part of the deck, and the lid back needs a faint gradient and a lit edge.

6) Clean corners and glass under a 5-10% push. All three screens have four visible, unobstructed corners. A centred 10% push keeps the insert's screen corners about 125 px from the side edges but only 64-68 px from the top and bottom; the case's lower corners come within about 35 px. It keeps tv's screen corners about 123 px from the right edge. In kitchen_over the shoulder and head lie outward of the screen corners, so a straight push moves them away. A sideways truck to the left would slide the near shoulder right, over the bottom-left corner. What breaks is not a corner:
(a) The grade's vignette takes the insert's screen, a flat 144 in the raw, from about 142 at the centre to 83-92 at the corners (35-42%). If the push is applied to graded stills, as in the 2.5D method, the vignette travels with the picture. Push the composited raw first, then grade.
(b) In depth-parallax pushes, the three big near occluders open holes with nothing behind them: the black lid in kitchen, Dawn's shoulder in kitchen_over, and the chair in tv. None has a clean background layer.
(c) The insert's glass reflection is a flat, slatless trapezoid at up to 62/255 (blue channel; about 50 luma) across the left-centre of the screen. Over NBC footage it will read as a smear.

7) Screen centre median 192 and palm-rest p95 104: confirmed within noise. I get 197 median on a 120x100 centre patch, and the palm rest at 84 median (p95 about 99).

fixes.problem: Phantom foreground chair. "tv foreground chair" is hidden in every other framing. It stands 0.5 m from where round 2 removed chair_n2 to clear the dining wide, so its back would land in that wide's lower centre, and here it reads as a sofa back. The camera hovers 27 cm above the dining table, inside its footprint, so the room's defining object is never seen.
fixes.fix: In build(), delete `_STATE["tv_chair"] = st.dining_chair("tv foreground chair", ...)` and the hide_render loop in apply_camera. Put the tv camera at a real seat. chair_s1 (2.48, 0.5, -90) faces the TV wall, and a seated eye there sits behind the table's near edge (y 0.485): CAMERAS["tv"] = dict(loc=(2.42, 0.62, 1.18), aim=(1.85, -2.24, 1.04), lens=26, focus="fx_tv", fstop=4.0, ...). Projected, this puts the TV in the upper centre (about x 563-850, y 106-274) with the picture to its left. The table's far edge (y -0.485) becomes a soft strip along the bottom (about y 645-675). The foot chair's back may enter soft at the right edge; that is fine, because it exists in every angle. (The first draft's loc (2.42, 0.42, 1.14), with aim z 1.36 and lens 28, still left the camera 6.5 cm inside the table's footprint and put the far edge about 150 px below the frame.) Re-solve the corner pins and re-check the dolly.

fixes.problem: Little says the light comes from the TV. The brightest wall (graded about 73) is under the picture, about 1 m from the TV's centre, where tv_return is aimed; the wall right of the TV grades about 21. With tv_spill's glossy visibility and specular both off, the brass candlesticks get no cool edge from the screen, and they throw no shadow away from it. The one screen-lit surface, a glow on the side wall just past the TV's end, starts 5-10 cm out from the corner behind a dark wedge, so it reads as detached.
fixes.fix: Centre st.area("tv_return") on the TV: loc (TV.x, -1.55, 1.40), aim (TV.x, -2.24, 1.25), size (1.1, 0.7), spread 120. Raise it until the wall within 20 cm of the case grades 45-55 and falls to under 30 about 50 cm out, so the picture sits darker than the TV's surround. (The picture's near edge is only 15 cm from the case.) Give tv_spill visible_glossy = True and data.specular_factor = 0.35, so the brass candlesticks pick up a cool edge on their TV side. Do not expect a streak on the sideboard top: from this eye line, 15 cm above the top, it reflects the wall just above it, not the screen. Trim d_sky to 0.10 in the tv framing so the picture wall drops away from the TV. Keep the side-wall glow. It is most likely tv_spill itself (confirm with one render at tv_spill 0). Widen tv_spill's spread from 150 to 180 so the glow runs into the corner and joins the TV.

fixes.problem: The TV reads as a second blank picture. It is about the same size as the framed print and hangs at nearly the same height beside it. About four-fifths of its width is past the sideboard's end, over bare wall, and the case casts no shadow.
fixes.fix: In home_set, swap the two. Centre the television over the sideboard (TV = (2.7, D["y0"] + 0.055, 1.62)) and move the framed print off the sideboard's -X end at z 1.55. Keep the TV's centre near 1.6 m. At 1.42 its bottom edge (about 1.14 m) would drop behind the candlesticks, whose wax tops stand at 1.28 m at x 2.25 and 2.45, inside the TV's new span (2.23-3.17); they would cut across the screen and its matte. The alternative is to move the candlesticks off that span. The swap also puts the dark TV (emission 0.004 outside the tv framing) where the print now sits, at the top right of chair and chair_gene, on the side the empty chair faces, which ties ch09 to ch10. Re-render those two frames and check the dining wide. For the case's depth, give it a contact shadow on the wall. Either add a soft dark decal 3-4 cm wide hugging its bottom and far edges, the way contact_shadows() does for the chairs, or bring tv_return in from above so the 44 mm case throws a real shadow below it. A black box hidden behind the case, as first suggested, could not be seen.

fixes.problem: The glass pass reflects a flat, slatless trapezoid at up to 62/255 (blue; about 50 luma) across the left-centre of the screen. Over NBC footage it will be a grey smear, and it contradicts the venetian blinds that define the room.
fixes.fix: The reflected ray from the screen lands on the foot-end wall at about y 0.9, inside its window (y 0.65-1.85). So the likely source is d_sky_end: it sits 8 cm inside that window, in front of its blind, and keeps glossy visibility; only its d_table_sky copy has visible_glossy = False. Confirm with a glossy-only render, then set d_sky_end.visible_glossy = False so the window backdrop and blind slats reflect instead and the reflection carries thin horizontal bars. If the backdrop itself is the source, check that the blind slats are not excluded from glossy rays. Cap the composite so the glass adds at most 25/255 over the footage. Repeat for the tv room view, where the same patch, from the same window, sits at the screen's lower-left corner.

fixes.problem: A near-frontal (11 degrees off the screen's normal, 9% keystone) 16:9 card with nothing else in frame. With footage in it, it reads as a picture-in-picture graphic, not a TV in a room.
fixes.fix: Swing the camera 10-15 degrees further round the TV and widen to lens 45, so the near case side shows as a thin edge. With the TV where it is now, loc (2.30, -0.80, 1.35), aimed 0.2 m toward +X of st.TV (1.82, -2.245, 1.57) at f/4, does this when projected. The screen fills about 45% of the frame, the case corners sit at least 38 px in, and candle0's wax tip enters soft at the bottom-left (about x 170, y 686), clear of the screen; the picture frame's edge also comes in at x 170-200. The first draft's numbers fail. From (2.25, -0.75, 1.55) the screen covers 45%, not 55%, and no candle enters the frame. Lowering the aim 8 cm pushes the screen's top-left corner off frame. If fix 3 moves the TV, re-solve against its new position. Re-export the corners and matte.

fixes.problem: The laptop lid back is raw 0.0 (graded 4-7) over about 5% of the frame, 7% with the unlit table under it: no light, no edge, a cut-out. It does not match the 84-grey deck seen in kitchen_over. Her right index points straight down from a raised hand, the one finger reaching the deck.
fixes.fix: The lid is already M["alu"] (0.155 grey, roughness 0.51) with a 3 mm bevel. It reads as a hole because nothing lights its back, so do not darken the material. Add a small area light (0.3 x 0.05 m, about 0.6 W, cool) behind and above the lid, aimed so only the lid's top bevel and upper left catch it, and light-link it to lap_lid only. Target a raw 8-15 gradient across the lid back with a raw 40-60 top-edge line. For the hand: CURL gives the right index (15, 27, 12) against the middle finger's (8, 12, 6), so the index alone reaches down. Bring index and middle to about the same curl and lower the wrist, so two finger pads rest on the pad together.

fixes.problem: The keyboard reads pale. The key tops grade about 100-115, a little above the deck (84), and the gaps between them grade 160-175. The keyboard well uses M["bezel"], which is near-black but glossy (roughness 0.08-0.14, specular 0.5), so it mirrors the lit screen as a pale grid, plus a pale rectangle where the arrow cluster leaves the well bare. Her left hand lies with its fingers straight out, the index straightest.
fixes.fix: Give lap_well its own matte near-black material (base about 0.01, roughness 0.6-0.7, specular about 0.2) instead of the glossy bezel glass. Lower the keycaps' specular from 0.4 to about 0.2; their base, 0.018 at roughness 0.55, is already darker than the deck's 0.070. Target: gaps darker than the key tops, and key tops at or below the deck. In CURL, curl all four left fingers 15-25 degrees (the left index is now only 5, 8, 6) and lower the left wrist target 5 mm. Then re-check both kitchen angles: the right hand must read on the trackpad here too, or move it to the keys in both angles and drop the trackpad.

fixes.problem: Under the 2.5D depth-parallax push, the near occluders (the lid, Dawn's shoulder, the tv foreground) open holes. The grade's vignette (35-42% at the insert's screen corners) travels with the picture if the push is applied after grading.
fixes.fix: For each of these cameras, render a second layer with the foreground hidden from the camera (visible_camera = False) as a clean background plate, saved next to the matte as <cam>.bg.png. In kitchen, hide lap_lid, lap_bezel and lap_screen together: with only the lid hidden, the bezel's black back still covers the frame, and the emission-only screen plane glows from both sides. In kitchen_over, hide Dawn's holder and children; in tv, hide the new table-edge foreground. In the animatic, push the composited raw first, then apply grade A, so the vignette stays fixed to the lens.

fixes.problem: The picture frame's bars butt with visible offsets: the top bar overruns a notched right stile, and the bottom bar overruns the left one. It reads as four sticks, and a push will show it.
fixes.fix: Build the frame as one ring. Create the outer rectangle with bmesh create_grid, inset the face by the moulding width, and delete the inner face. Extrude it the current 40 mm toward the room, then bevel the outer and inner edges 3 mm with 2 segments. That gives mitred corners in one mesh. Keep the mat and print as they are.

fixes.problem: The under-cabinet strip (graded max 133, the frame's brightest line) runs about 45 px above Dawn's head, a near tangent that pulls the eye off her face.
fixes.fix: Dim the k_ucLens glow from 2.2 to about 1.0. If the tangent still reads, raise the camera rather than re-aim it. A tilt moves the strip and her head together (aim z 1.04 to 1.00 leaves the gap unchanged and only pushes the strip toward the top edge). Raising loc z from 1.10 to 1.20 and aim z from 1.04 to 1.10 drops her head, at 2.2 m, about 35 px further from the strip at 4.1 m, while the strip stays where it is in frame. The cost is that the lens moves from a little below her eyes to her eye line. Keep the strip's whole length inside the frame.
